title: Singapore to KL Bus: Arriving at Lalaport BBCC (2026)
metaDescription: Taking the bus from Singapore to KL? Where coaches arrive, the border and MDAC, the Lalaport hub's lockers and trains, and your ride back.

contentBlocks.content: An express coach from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur takes about five to six hours, including the stop at the border. Many coaches now end at the Lalaport Transportation Hub, an indoor coach terminal under the LaLaport BBCC mall in Bukit Bintang that opened in July 2026. The hub is open 24 hours and connects to the Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail stations, so you can be at a Bukit Bintang hotel within minutes of getting off. Not every Singapore to KL bus goes there, though. Some still end at TBS in Bandar Tasik Selatan, so check the arrival stop on your ticket before you pay.

This guide covers where Singapore coaches arrive in KL, what to check when you book, the border crossing, what is waiting for you at the Lalaport hub, and how to get to your hotel, the airport or Genting from there.
Key Takeaways
How long is the bus from Singapore to KL? About five to six hours, depending on traffic and the queue at the Causeway or Second Link. Fridays, weekends and school holidays are slower.

Where do Singapore buses arrive in KL? Many end at the Lalaport Transportation Hub in Bukit Bintang. Others end at TBS (Terminal Bersepadu Selatan), about 30 minutes' drive south of the city centre. Your ticket names the stop.

Do I need an MDAC on the bus? Singapore citizens do not. Singapore permanent residents and most other passport holders must submit a Malaysia Digital Arrival Card within 3 days before crossing, choosing LAND as the mode of travel.

What is at the Lalaport hub? An air conditioned waiting lounge, departure screens, 36 paid luggage lockers, ATMs and money changers, food on the same floor, and the Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail a short walk away.
How do I get back to Singapore? From the same hub. Coaches leave Lalaport for Bugis and more than 20 other Singapore stops, and you can book them on ttklia.com.
Where Singapore coaches arrive in Kuala Lumpur

Singapore coaches arrive at one of a few places in KL, and the one on your ticket decides how your first hour goes. Booking sites often show the route as just "Kuala Lumpur", which tells you nothing. Open the trip details until you see a named stop.

Arrival stopWhere it isGood for
Lalaport Transportation Hub (LaLaport BBCC)Level LG1, East Atrium of the LaLaport BBCC mall, Bukit Bintang. Linked to the Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail.Hotels in Bukit Bintang, Pudu, Chinatown and KLCC. Indoor, open 24 hours.
TBS (Terminal Bersepadu Selatan)Bandar Tasik Selatan, south of the city centre, about 30 minutes by car.Stays in the south of KL, or onward buses to other states.
Other city stopsSome operators use their own stops, such as Berjaya Times Square.Check the exact meeting point with the operator.

The Lalaport hub opened in July 2026 to give Singapore coaches a proper place to stop in the city centre. Before that, passengers were often let off at the roadside near Berjaya Times Square. It can handle up to 200 coach trips a day, about 150 of them to or from Singapore (The Straits Times), and around 30 operators run from its 11 bus bays (LaLaport BBCC).
Booking your Singapore to KL bus: check these before you pay
The "from" fare in a search result is rarely what you end up paying, and the arrival stop matters as much as the price. Before you pay, check five things on the trip details:

• Boarding point in Singapore. Coaches leave from places such as Golden Mile, Kovan, Woodlands and Jurong East. Pick the one closest to you.
  • Arrival stop in KL. Look for "Lalaport", "LaLaport BBCC" or "Bukit Bintang" if you are staying in the city centre.
  • Departure time. Morning coaches avoid the evening queues at the Causeway. Late night departures arrive in KL in the early hours, which the 24 hour hub handles well.
  • Total at checkout. Compare the final price including fees, not the "from" price.
  • Name on the ticket. It must match your passport.
Fares change by operator, date and coach class, so compare on the day you book. Save the ticket to your phone; you may be asked for it at the border and when you get back on.
Crossing the border by coach

You get off the coach twice on the way to KL: once at the Singapore checkpoint to clear departure, and once at the Malaysian checkpoint, where you take your luggage through immigration and customs. Keep your passport, phone, ticket and any medicine with you. Note the coach's number plate and colour before you get off, so you can find it again on the other side. Coaches do not wait long for slow passengers.

If you are not a Singapore citizen, submit your Malaysia Digital Arrival Card before you leave home. It opens 3 days before your crossing; choose LAND as the mode of travel and type the coach operator's name or trip number where the form asks for a transport number. Our MDAC guide walks through every field.
Singapore citizens do not need an MDAC at any Malaysian entry point, including the land crossings.
Arriving at the Lalaport Transportation Hub

When your coach pulls in, you step off inside the building, not at the roadside. The hub is on Level LG1 of the East Atrium of LaLaport BBCC and is open 24 hours (The Straits Times). What you will find there:

• Luggage lockers. 36 lockers near the bus bays, RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours depending on size, and you can open them as often as you like within that time. Handy if you arrive before hotel check in.
  • Waiting lounge. Air conditioned seating with power sockets and departure screens.
  • Cash. ATMs and money changers on the same floor, so you can change your Singapore dollars into ringgit before you leave the mall.
  • Food. Ramen, Japanese curry and Korean barbecue restaurants on the lower floors, and a CU convenience store for something quick.
  • Your SIM. If you booked a Teeko travel SIM, you can collect it at the tour centre at Lalaport BBCC, so your phone works before you head into the city. The exact counter details come with your booking.
  • Toilets and prayer rooms. Clean toilets in the hub, and separate surau for men and women on Level LG.
The hub itself never closes, but the mall's shops and restaurants keep normal mall hours. If your coach arrives at 3 AM, the convenience store and the lockers are what you have.
From Lalaport to your hotel

The Hang Tuah LRT and Monorail interchange connects to LaLaport BBCC through a link bridge on Level 1, so most of central KL is one train ride away. Buy a token at the station machine with a card or cash.

Going toHow
Bukit Bintang and PavilionMonorail from Hang Tuah to Bukit Bintang station, one stop. Or walk, about 15 minutes.
KLCC and the Petronas Twin TowersMonorail to Bukit Bintang, then the covered walkway from Pavilion, about 1 km.
Petaling Street and ChinatownLRT from Hang Tuah to Plaza Rakyat. Merdeka MRT station is also a short walk from the mall.
KL SentralMonorail from Hang Tuah to the end of the line at KL Sentral.
Anywhere, with luggageBook Grab or a taxi and set the pickup to LaLaport Drop Off 2, the mall's closest pickup point to the hub.
Arrived hungry? Bukit Bintang is the right place for it. Our supper spots in Kuala Lumpur guide covers late night food within reach of the hub, and the restaurant directory has the rest of the city.
Your next ride from the same hub
The Lalaport hub is also where you leave from, which saves a trip across town at the end of your stay. The hub is run by ttklia.com, which sells these routes:

• Back to Singapore. Coaches from Lalaport to Bugis and more than 20 other Singapore stops, including HarbourFront, Woodlands, Jurong East, Tampines and Resorts World Sentosa.
  • To the airport. If you are flying out of KL, the Lalaport to KLIA2 bus leaves from the same bays. Shuttle vans also run to KLIA Terminal 1.
  • To Genting Highlands. Hire a car with a driver for 8 or 10 hours and do Genting as a day trip from Bukit Bintang.

contentBlocks.content: Frequently Asked Questions
How long does the bus from Singapore to KL take?

The bus from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur takes about five to six hours, including immigration at both checkpoints. Allow more on Friday evenings, weekends and school holidays, when the queues at the Causeway and Second Link are longest.
Do I need an MDAC if I live in Singapore?

Singapore citizens do not need an MDAC to enter Malaysia by land. Singapore permanent residents and other foreign nationals do, unless they hold a Malaysian Long Term Pass; submit it within 3 days before crossing and choose LAND as the mode of travel.
Is the Lalaport Transportation Hub open at night?

Yes. The Lalaport Transportation Hub is open 24 hours, so late night and early morning coaches can arrive and leave there. The mall's shops and restaurants keep normal hours, so plan food around that.
Can I leave my luggage at Lalaport?
Yes. The hub has 36 paid luggage lockers near the bus bays, from RM20 to RM55 for 24 hours depending on size, and you can open yours as many times as you need within that period.
Can I book Singapore to Lalaport on ttklia.com?

Not yet. ttklia.com sells coaches from Lalaport to Singapore, but not from Singapore to Lalaport, so book your journey into KL with a bus operator or booking site and book your return from the hub on ttklia.com.
Conclusion

For the Singapore to KL bus, pick a coach that names the Lalaport Transportation Hub as its arrival stop if you are staying anywhere central. You step off indoors in Bukit Bintang, with lockers, cash and trains a few minutes away. Sort your MDAC before you leave if you are not a Singapore citizen. And when it is time to go home, you leave from the same place: book your coach from Lalaport back to Singapore on ttklia.com.
